citacoes.trecho: Code generation aims to automatically generate the source code given a natural language requirement [7, 18, 30].
In this paper, we propose a novel learning-based selection approach named LAIL (LLM-Aware In-context Learning) for code generation.
Based on the labeled data, we import a contrastive learning objective to train an effective retriever that acquires the preference of LLMs in code generation.
Given a test requirement, the optimized retriever selects several examples as a prompt that is inputted to LLMs for code generation (C).
The input of LLMs only contains a prompt and a test requirement without any natural language instructions.
Zero-Shot Learning [11] directly inputs a requirement into LLMs without any examples as the prompt.
Random [14] randomly select a few examples from the training set and construct a prompt.
In inference, it first generates test cases and then predicts programs. For a fair comparison, we use the same pipeline to LAIL and all baselines.
Finally, it treats the k nearest examples as a prompt.
The approach computes the uncertainty of each candidate and selects k items with high perplexity as a prompt.
Some heuristic methods that select the same examples as prompts for all test requirements are not optimal for ICL.
The Match-BLEU format uses the BLEU score of the generated program to measure examples.

However, ICL comes along with the robustness problem [33], which is sensitive to the selected examples in prompts, resulting in the performance usually varying from almost random to near state-of-the-art performance.
Although one may remedy it by inputting more examples in the prompt, it is highly impractical due to the limited input length of LLMs.
Modeling on the full space of the training set is quadratic and thus prohibitive.
To mitigate this limitation, we introduce a two-stage process to estimate examples in the training set.
The learning rate is 5e-5 and the batch size is 32. We train the retriever for about 1 hour on 4 NVIDIA A100.
We can find that the more hard negative examples, the worse our approach performs.
There are two main threats to the validity of our work.
For LLMs (e.g., GPT-3.5 and ChatGPT), the hyper-parameters (e.g., temperature) of sampling will impact their outputs.
In addition, the performance of LLMs heavily depends on the prompts, including the instruction and the number of examples.
To alleviate this threat, we leverage the same number of examples for all approaches and directly construct prompts without any natural language instructions.
To ensure fairness, we execute each method three times and report the average experimental results.
For a fair comparison, we set the same parameters to generate programs for all baselines and our LAIL.
Thus, we use the training set of each dataset as the candidate set for all approaches in this paper and believe that the training set can provide supporting examples for test requirements.
For baselines, we apply the source code and parameters published by their original papers [21, 40, 47].
We do not tune the prompt and hyper-parameters experimentally and set them empirically.
In this paper, we leverage the largest version with 16 billion parameters (i.e. CodeGen-Multi-16B).
In this paper, we use OpenAI’s APIs to access the latest version with 175 billion parameters (i.e., text-davinci-003).
We leverage OpenAI’s APIs to access ChatGPT (i.e., gpt-3.5-turbo).
Finally, the percentage of solved requirements in all test requirements is treated as Pass@k.

Método, bases, divisões, parâmetros de decodificação e de treino do recuperador são descritos, mas o número padrão de exemplos no prompt não é informado, o pipeline comum ('same pipeline') é ambíguo quanto à geração de testes, o LLM de feedback do recuperador nas Tabelas 2 e 3 não é explicitado e a amostra da avaliação humana é inconsistente (50 por base × 3 vs. 400 programas).

Versões dos modelos (CodeGen-Multi-16B, text-davinci-003, gpt-3.5-turbo), hiperparâmetros de decodificação e de treino são informados; faltam o número padrão de exemplos, datas de acesso às APIs, estimador de Pass@k e qualquer link para código ou dados; o DOI impresso é marcador de template.

O estudo não discute contaminação de dados (vazamento das bases MBPP/MBJP/MBCPP no pré-treinamento dos LLMs). Os exemplos do prompt vêm do conjunto de treino, separado do conjunto de teste, mas o estudo não apresenta essa divisão como controle de contaminação.
